words: We sent Timothy, our brother and fellow worker for God in the gospel of Christ,

sides.label: Timothy comes later to Corinth
words: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia,

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on First Thessalonians, No. IV, says the sending back of Timothy accounts for his late arrival at Corinth. Barnes, on 1 Thessalonians 3:2, makes the same point.

cites.quote: The sending back of Timothy into Macedonia accounts also for his not coming to Corinth till after Paul ... had been fixed in that city some considerable time. ... If this was the first time of their coming up with him after their separation at Berea, there is nothing to account for a delay so contrary to what appears from the history itself to have been St. Paul's plan and expectation.
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: Fourthly, the sending back of Timothy to Macedonia, as mentioned in the Epistle, is a circumstance which will account for the fact mentioned in Act 18:5 , that Timothy came to him "at Corinth," instead of at Athens.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: Jews began it, their own countrymen carried it out
patterns.about: The letter says the church suffered from its own countrymen, as the churches of Judea did from the Jews. Acts shows the same pattern: unbelieving Jews start the trouble, but they stir up the crowds and the Gentiles of the city to carry it out.

sides.label: From your own countrymen
words: You suffered from your own countrymen the very things they suffered from the Jews,

sides.label: A mob at Thessalonica
words: So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar.

sides.label: The crowds at Berea
words: they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.

sides.label: The Gentiles at Iconium
words: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on First Thessalonians, No. V, sets this verse beside Acts 17:5, 17:13 and 14:2. Henry, Clarke and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, each on 1 Thessalonians 2:14, say the Jews led the persecution and stirred up others to do it.

cites.quote: The epistle therefore represents the case accurately as the history states it. It was the Jews always who set on foot the persecutions against the apostles and their followers. ... But out of Judea it was at the hands of the Gentiles
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: In every city where the apostles went to preach the gospel the Jews stirred up the inhabitants against them. They were the ringleaders of persecution in all places; so in particular it was at Thessalonica: Act 17:5
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: It is worthy of remark that, in almost every case, the Jews were the leaders of all persecutions against the apostles and the infant Church. And what they could not do themselves, they instigated others to do
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: including primarily the Jews settled at Thessalonica, from whom the persecution originated, and also the Gentiles there, instigated by the Jews
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: Worked night and day, not just three Sabbaths
patterns.about: Acts names only three Sabbaths in the synagogue at Thessalonica, yet the letter recalls Paul working night and day among them. Elsewhere Acts shows him leaving the synagogue and teaching on for a long time, which suits a longer stay here too.

sides.label: Working night and day
words: We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to anyone while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.

sides.label: Three Sabbaths in the synagogue
words: and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

sides.label: Synagogue first, then onward
words: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months,
This continued for two years,

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on First Thessalonians, No. VI, answers this seeming gap from Paul's way at Corinth and Ephesus. Jamieson-Fausset-Brown on 1 Thessalonians 2:9 and Barnes in his opening to the letter also say the three Sabbaths were only his time in the synagogue.

cites.quote: Upon inspecting the history, I see nothing in it which negatives the supposition that St. Paul pursued the same plan at Thessalonica which he adopted in other places ; and that, though he resorted to the synagogue only three sabbath days, yet he remained in the city, and in the exercise of his ministry amongst the Gentile citizens, much longer
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: Though but "three Sabbaths" are mentioned, Act 17:2 , these refer merely to the time of his preaching to the Jews in the synagogue.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: In the epistle Th1 2:9 , Paul says that when he was among them, he "labored night and day, because he would not be chargeable unto any of them, and preached unto them the gospel of God" (compare Th2 3:8 ), which looks as if he had been with them a longer time than the "three sabbaths,"
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: Paid his own way, as only Philippi gave to him
patterns.about: Writing to Thessalonica, Paul says he ate no one's food without paying and worked night and day. Writing to Philippi, he says that in those early days no church but theirs gave to him, even while he was in Thessalonica.

sides.label: Ate no one's food unpaid
words: nor did we eat anyone’s food without paying for it.

sides.label: No church but you
words: no church but you partnered with me in the matter of giving and receiving.
For even while I was in Thessalonica, you provided for my needs again and again.

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Second Thessalonians, No. II, sets this verse beside Philippians 4:15. Clarke on Philippians 4:16 and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown on 2 Thessalonians 3:8 join his own work at Thessalonica to the gifts from Philippi.

cites.quote: As St. Paul tells the Philippians " that no church communicated with him, as concerning giving and receiving, but they only," he could not, consistently with the truth of this declaration, have received any thing from the neighboring church of Thessalonica.
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: While labouring to plant the Church there, he was supported partly by working with his hands, Th1 2:9 ; Th2 3:7-9 ; and partly by the contributions sent him from Philippi.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: The Philippians did not regard it as a burden to contribute to his support ( Phi 4:15-16 ), sending to him while he was in this very Thessalonica
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: Worked with his hands to set an example
patterns.about: Paul tells the Thessalonians he worked night and day to give them an example to follow. In Acts he tells the Ephesian elders that his own hands met his needs, and that by such hard work he showed them how to help the weak. Same practice, same purpose, different words.

sides.label: An example for you to imitate
words: we wanted to offer ourselves as an example for you to imitate.

sides.label: These hands of mine
words: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.
In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak,

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Second Thessalonians, No. II, sets this verse beside Paul's words at Miletus in Acts 20:34, finding the same practice and the same purpose told in different words.

cites.quote: The sentiment in the epistle and in the speech is in both parts of it so much alike, and yet the words which convey it show so little of imitation or even of resemblance, that the agreement cannot well be explained without supposing the speech and the letter to have really proceeded from the same person.
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

patterns.short: A second letter to correct a misreading of the first
patterns.about: The first letter speaks of those alive at the Lord's coming and of that day coming like a thief. The second asks the church not to be alarmed by any message or letter seeming to be from Paul that says the day has already come.

sides.label: Do not be alarmed
words: not to be easily disconcerted or alarmed by any spirit or message or letter seeming to be from us, alleging that the Day of the Lord has already come.

sides.label: We who are alive and remain
words: we who are alive and remain until the coming of the Lord will by no means precede those who have fallen asleep.

sides.label: Like a thief
words: But you, brothers, are not in the darkness so that this day should overtake you like a thief.

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Second Thessalonians, No. III, reads 2 Thessalonians 2:2 as correcting a misreading of 1 Thessalonians 4:15-17 and 5:4. Clarke and Barnes on 2 Thessalonians 2:1 and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown in his opening to the letter say the same.

cites.quote: It should seem that the Thessalonians, or some, however, amongst them, had from this passage conceived an opinion (and that not very unnaturally) that the coming of Christ was to take place instantly ... The apostle therefore now writes, amongst other purposes, to quiet this alarm, and to rectify the misconstruction
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: It is evident that the Thessalonians, incited by deceived or false teachers, had taken a wrong meaning out of the words of the first epistle, Th1 4:15 , etc., concerning the day of judgment; and were led then to conclude that that day was at hand
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: In regard to that great event of which I spoke to you in my former epistle - the coming of the Saviour - I beseech you not to be troubled, as if it were soon to happen. As his views had been misunderstood or misrepresented, he now proposes to show them that there was nothing in the true doctrine which should create alarm
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: The apostle's description of Christ's sudden second coming ( Th1 4:13 , &c., and Th1 5:2 ), and the possibility of its being at any time, led them to believe it was actually at hand.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: Gathered to Him, as the first letter told
patterns.about: The second letter speaks of the Lord's coming and our being gathered together to Him. The first letter had described that very gathering: the dead rising first and the living caught up together with them to meet the Lord in the air.

sides.label: Gathered together to Him
words: Now concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered together to Him, we ask you, brothers,

sides.label: Caught up together
words: we who are alive and remain will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air.

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Second Thessalonians, No. III, item 2, takes the gathering in 2 Thessalonians 2:1 from 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17. Barnes and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, both on 2 Thessalonians 2:1, point to the same verse.

cites.quote: Now in the first epistle the description of the coming of Christ is accompanied with the mention of this very circumstance of his saints being collected round him. ... This I suppose to be the " gathering together unto him" intended in the second epistle ; and that the author, when he used these words, retained in his thoughts what he had written on the subject before.
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: And by our gathering together unto him - There is manifest allusion here to what is said in the First Epistle Th1 4:17 , "then we shall be caught up together with them in the clouds;"
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: our gathering together unto him--the consummating or final gathering together of the saints to Him at His coming, as announced, Mat 24:31 ; Th1 4:17 .
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: A letter seeming to be from us, and three names
patterns.about: The second letter warns against a letter seeming to be from us. The first letter carried the names of Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, so the words may point back to it. Many take them instead to mean a forged letter, so this reading is uncertain.

sides.label: A letter seeming to be from us
words: or letter seeming to be from us,

sides.label: Paul, Silvanus and Timothy
words: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, To the church of the Thessalonians

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Second Thessalonians, No. III, item 3, suggests the words point to the first letter, which bore the three names. He grants that many expositors read them of a forged letter instead.

cites.quote: Now this circumstance, which is a very close one, belongs to the epistle at present in our hands ; for the epistle which we call the First Epistle to the Thessalonians contains these names in its superscription.
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

patterns.short: Zealous for the law, in his speech and in his letter
patterns.about: In Acts Paul tells the crowd he was trained at the feet of Gamaliel in the law of the fathers and was zealous for God. In his letter he says he was advancing in Judaism and was extremely zealous for the traditions of his fathers.

sides.label: Zealous for the law of the fathers
words: I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers.
I am just as zealous for God as any of you here today.

sides.label: Zealous for his fathers' traditions
words: I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries and was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Galatians, No. II, sets Paul's own account of his early zeal in the letter beside his speech in Acts 22. Barnes on Acts 22:3 points to Galatians 1:14 for the same zeal.

cites.quote: St. Paul in the early part of his life had addicted himself to the study of the Jewish religion, and was distinguished by his zeal for the institution, and for the traditions which had been incorporated with it.
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: And was zealous toward God - Gal 1:14 . He had a constant burning zeal for God and His Law, which was expressed not only by scrupulous adherence to its forms, but by persecuting all who opposed it
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: The persecutor Acts describes, in his own words
patterns.about: Acts tells how Saul went from house to house dragging believers off to prison. In his letter Paul reminds the Galatians that they had heard how severely he persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.

sides.label: Going from house to house
words: But Saul began to destroy the church.
Going from house to house, he dragged off men and women and put them in prison.

sides.label: How severely I persecuted
words: how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Galatians, No. II, sets Acts 8:3 beside Galatians 1:13. Barnes on Galatians 1:13 sends the reader to Acts 8:3, and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown on Acts 8:3 lists Galatians 1:13 among Paul's own confessions.

cites.quote: St. Paul, before his conversion, had been a fierce persecutor of the new sect. ... This is the history of St. Paul, as delivered in the Acts : in the recital of his own history in the epistle
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: I persecuted the church - See Act 8:3 ; Act 9:1 ff.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: haling men and women, &c.--See his own affecting confessions afterwards ( Act 22:4 ; Act 26:9-10 ; Co1 15:9 ; Gal 1:13 ; Phi 3:6 ; Ti1 1:13 ).
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: Returned to Damascus, where Acts places his call
patterns.about: The letter tells of God calling Paul and revealing His Son in him, but names no place. Only a passing word at the end, that he later returned to Damascus, places the call there. Acts says the light from heaven met him as he drew near to Damascus.

sides.label: Near Damascus
words: As Saul drew near to Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.

sides.label: Called, then returned to Damascus
words: called me by His grace
later returned to Damascus.

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Galatians, No. II, notes that only the passing word about returning fixes the call at Damascus. Barnes on Galatians 1:17 calls Damascus the place where Paul was converted, and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown on 1:15 ties the call to Acts 9:3-8.

cites.quote: In this quotation from the epistle, I desire to be remarked how incidentally it appears that the affair passed at Damascus. ... a casual expression at the end, and an expression brought in for a different purpose, alone fixes it to have been at Damascus
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: And returned again unto Damascus - He did not go to Jerusalem to consult with the apostles after his visit to Arabia, but returned again to the place where he was converted and preached there
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: called me--on the way to Damascus ( Act 9:3-8 ).
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: He began to preach at once, as both accounts say
patterns.about: Acts says Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues of Damascus. The letter says God revealed His Son in him so that he might preach Him, and that he did not stop to consult anyone first.

sides.label: Promptly proclaiming Jesus
words: Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues

sides.label: That I might preach Him
words: to reveal His Son in me so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood,

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Galatians, No. II, notes that both accounts have Paul preaching straight after his call. Jamieson-Fausset-Brown on Galatians 1:16 and Henry on Acts 9:20 set the two verses together.

cites.quote: It also draws the agreement between the two quotations somewhat closer, to observe that they both state St. Paul to have preached the Gospel immediately upon his call
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: It denotes the sudden fitness of the apostle. So Act 9:20 , "Straightway he preached Christ in the synagogue."
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: He preached Christ in the synagogues, Act 9:20 . To this he had an extraordinary call, and for it an extraordinary qualification, God having immediately revealed his Son to him and in him, that he might preach him, Gal 1:15 , Gal 1:16 .
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: Syria, then Cilicia, on the way to Tarsus
patterns.about: Acts says the brothers took Paul down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus. The letter says he then went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia, Tarsus being in Cilicia: the order in which a traveller would come to them on the way north to Tarsus.

sides.label: Sent off to Tarsus
words: they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

sides.label: Syria and Cilicia
words: Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Galatians, No. II, shows the order Syria then Cilicia fits the journey to Tarsus in Acts 9:30. Jamieson-Fausset-Brown on Acts 9:30 also reads Galatians 1:21 as this journey, through Antioch into Cilicia.

cites.quote: The history had told us that Paul passed from Cæsarea to Tarsus : if he took this journey by land, it would carry him through Syria into Cilicia ; and he would come, after his visit to Jerusalem, " into the regions of Syria and Cilicia," in the very order in which he mentions them in the epistle.
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: Why the churches of Judea come up on that journey
patterns.about: Right after saying he went to Syria and Cilicia, Paul adds that the churches of Judea did not know him by face and only heard about him. One reading takes this as a hint that he passed hastily through Judea on the journey from Caesarea to Tarsus that Acts describes.

sides.label: Down to Caesarea, off to Tarsus
words: they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

sides.label: Unknown to the churches of Judea
words: I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
They only heard the account

patterns.evidence: Paley, Horae Paulinae, on Galatians, No. II, argues the mention of the Judean churches makes sense if Paul crossed Judea by land on the way from Caesarea. Jamieson-Fausset-Brown on Galatians 1:21 reads it the other way, as a sea journey, so this stays one view.

cites.quote: the passage itself has little significancy, and that the connection is inexplicable, unless St. Paul went through Judea* (though probably by a hasty journey) at the time that he came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

patterns.short: Barnabas at Antioch with Paul, as Acts has him
patterns.about: In the letter Barnabas is at Antioch with Paul when Peter draws back from the Gentiles, and is led astray too. Acts often has Barnabas with Paul at Antioch: a full year teaching there, a long stay after their journey, and again after the meeting at Jerusalem.

words: When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face
so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.

sides.label: A full year at Antioch
words: he brought him back to Antioch. So for a full year they met together with the church

sides.label: A long time there
words: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch
And they spent a long time there with the disciples.

sides.label: Remained at Antioch
words: But Paul and Barnabas remained at Antioch

cites.quote: Barnabas was with St. Paul at Antioch. ... Now what says the epistle ?
cites.read: the 1849 text in the CC0 transcription at github.com/nick-lang/undesigned-coincidences-paley-blunt (commit c529753)

cites.quote: Paul also, and Barnabas, continued in Antioch - How long a time is unknown. It is probable that at this time the unhappy incident occurred between Paul and Peter which is recorded in Gal 2:11-14 .

cites.quote: How rich must Antioch at this time have been in the ministrations of the Gospel! (For a painful scene on this occasion between Paul and Peter, see Gal 2:11-14 ).
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: Jerusalem was where the apostles were to be found
patterns.about: Paul says he did not go up to Jerusalem to the apostles before him, as if everyone knew that was where they were. Acts says that when the church was scattered all except the apostles left Jerusalem, and later sends Paul and Barnabas up to the apostles there.

words: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the apostles who came before me,

sides.label: All except the apostles scattered
words: all except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.

sides.label: Up to Jerusalem to the apostles
words: to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.

sides.label: James, the Lord's brother
words: James, the Lord’s brother.

sides.label: James the brother of John killed
words: He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.

sides.label: James speaks at Jerusalem
words: James declared, “Brothers, listen to me!

parts.label: Those on board are struck with fear

words.storm: Then the LORD hurled a great wind upon the sea
words.danger: that the ship was in danger of breaking apart.
words.asleep: where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
words.woken: How can you sleep? Get up and call upon your God.
words.cargo: And they threw the ship’s cargo into the sea to lighten the load.
words.calm: and the raging sea grew calm.
words.fear: Then the men feared the LORD greatly

words.storm: Soon a violent windstorm came up
words.danger: so that it was being swamped.
words.asleep: But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion.
words.woken: So they woke Him and said

words.storm: a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.
words.cargo: the men began to jettison the cargo.
words.danger: we abandoned all hope of being saved.

patterns.evidence: Henry, on Jonah 1:4-5, likens the sailors throwing out the cargo to Paul's sailors in Acts 27, and on Acts 27 likens the wind and the cargo to Jonah's. Henry on Mark 4 likens the disciples' fear to the fear of Jonah's sailors, and on Matthew 8:24 sets Jesus' sleep beside Jonah's. Pusey in Barnes' Notes on Jonah 1:15 sets the sea stilled there beside the Lord rebuking the sea.

cites.quote: They cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them, as Paul's mariners in a like case cast forth even the tackling of the ship, and the wheat, Act 27:18 , Act 27:19 , Act 27:38 .

cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: this was a sleep, not of security, like Jonah's in a storm, but of holy serenity, and dependence upon his Father

patterns.short: The temple courts cleared, at the start and the end
patterns.about: Early in His work and again in His last week, Jesus goes into the temple courts, drives out the traders, overturns the money changers' tables and those selling doves, and says what His Father's house is meant to be.

parts.label: He goes up to the temple

words.drives: drove all from the temple courts
words.doves: To those selling doves He said
words.house: How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!

words.drives: began to drive out those who were buying and selling there.
words.tables: He overturned the tables of the money changers
words.doves: and the seats of those selling doves.
words.house: My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations

patterns.evidence: Albert Barnes, on John 2:14, says this clearing is in almost all respects like the one at the close of the ministry, and that the same scene was repeated three years later. Henry on Mark 11 sets the charge there beside the charge in John 2:16. Brown in the JFB heads Mark 11:15-18 the second cleansing of the temple.

cites.quote: The transaction here recorded is in almost all respects similar to that which has been explained in the notes at Mat 21:12 . This took place at the commencement of his public ministry; that at the close.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: Though Jesus thus purified the temple at the commencement of his ministry, yet in three years the same scene was to be repeated.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: When Christ drove out the buyers and sellers at the beginning of his ministry, he only charged them with making the temple a house of merchandise ( Joh 2:16 ); but now he chargeth them with making it a den of thieves

cites.quote: Second Cleansing of the Temple ( Mar 11:15-18 ).

patterns.about: The apostles are jailed under guard. In the night the doors open: once by an angel, once of themselves as an angel leads Peter out, once in an earthquake. In two of the tellings the chains fall away.

words.doors: At once all the doors flew open

patterns.short: What was kept back, and the death that followed
patterns.about: As Israel begins in the land and the church begins in Jerusalem, a man secretly keeps something back for himself: Achan from the things set apart for God, Ananias from the price he claimed to give. He is called to account, dies, and is buried.

words.kept: took some of what was set apart.
words.asked: I urge you to tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me.
words.died: And all Israel stoned him to death.
words.buried: And they heaped over Achan a large pile of rocks

words.kept: he kept back some of the proceeds for himself
words.asked: Ananias, how is it that Satan has filled your heart
words.buried: carried him out and buried him.

patterns.evidence: Espin in Barnes' Notes, on Joshua 7:1, says Achan's sin was the same as that of Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5. Brown in the JFB, on Acts 5:11, says the judgment and the sin had their counterpart in Achan, and the time, at a new beginning, was alike.

cites.quote: Achan in diverting any of these devoted things to his own purposes, committed the sin of sacrilege, that of Ananias and Sapphira. Act 5:2-3 .
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: This effect on the Christian community itself was the chief design of so startling a judgment; which had its counterpart, as the sin itself had, in Achan (Jos. 7:1-26), while the time--at the commencement of a new career--was similar.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

patterns.short: A foreign leper cleansed, who comes back
patterns.about: A leper is told to go and do something simple. On doing it he is made clean. The one who comes back to give thanks is a foreigner: a commander of Aram, and a Samaritan.

words.go: Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan
words.clean: and his flesh was restored and became like that of a little child, and he was clean.

words.clean: And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.
words.back: he came back, praising God in a loud voice.

cites.quote: Of the ten lepers that our Saviour cleansed, the only one that returned to give thanks was a Samaritan, Luk 17:16 . This Syrian did so

patterns.short: A child brought to the house of the LORD
patterns.about: Samuel and Jesus are each brought by their parents to the house of the LORD with an offering and given to Him. The parents are blessed, the family goes up each year, and the boy grows in favor with God and with people.

parts.label: Brought to the house of the LORD
The family goes up each year
He grows in favor with God and man

words.grew: and in favor with the LORD and with man.

words.given: to present Him to the Lord

patterns.short: A face shining from the mountain
patterns.about: On the mountain with God, the face of Moses becomes radiant, and the face of Jesus shines like the sun. Those with them are afraid, and each scene ends with the coming down from the mountain.

words.shine: his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD.
words.afraid: And they were afraid to approach him.

words.shine: His face shone like the sun
words.down: As they were coming down the mountain

Clarke on Exodus 34:29 thinks Moses then looked as at the Lord's transfiguration. Henry on Exodus 34 and Matthew 17 sets the two faces side by side.

cites.quote: We read of our Lord Jesus, not only that his face shone as the sun, but his whole body also, for his raiment was white and glistering, Luk 9:29 .

cites.quote: His face shone as the sun; that is, with a special brightness. A similar appearance is described respecting Moses when he came down from the mount, Exo 34:29-30 .

patterns.short: A mother's song when God gives a son
patterns.about: Hannah, after Samuel is given, and Mary, carrying Jesus, sing to God in much the same order: joy in the LORD, none holy like Him, the proud brought down, the hungry filled, the lowly lifted up, and His anointed or His servant Israel upheld.

words.holy: There is no one holy like the LORD.

words.people: He will exalt the horn of His anointed.

words.joy: and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior!

words.hungry: He has filled the hungry with good things
words.people: He has helped His servant Israel

patterns.evidence: Henry, on 1 Samuel 2:1, says Mary's song has great likeness to Hannah's, and on Luke 1 that it begins like Hannah's. Hervey in Barnes' Notes, on 1 Samuel 2:1, sets Hannah's song beside Mary's, and Albert Barnes on Luke 1:55 calls the likeness striking. Clarke, on Luke 1:46 and 1:53, calls Mary's song a counterpart of Hannah's.

cites.quote: The virgin Mary's song has great affinity with this of Hannah, Luk 1:46 .

cites.quote: It takes its place by the side of the songs of Miriam, Deborah, and the Virgin Mary

cites.quote: others think it better compared with the song of Hannah, upon the birth of Samuel, which, like this, passes from a family mercy to a public and general one. This begins, like that, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, Sa1 2:1 .
